intro: I study how AI and data change human judgment and organizational decisions. My research combines empirical analysis, causal and graph-based learning, and human–AI interaction.

themes.title: AI, Organizations, and Innovation
themes.question: How do AI and information environments change knowledge creation, sharing, and resource allocation?
themes.description: I study incentives, technological change and the relationships through which knowledge travels. This work connects research on organizations and innovation with emerging questions about AI-mediated markets and scientific work.

themes.title: Human–AI Interaction and Visual Analytics
themes.question: How can people understand, revise, and take responsibility for AI-supported decisions?
themes.description: We develop and study interfaces that make complex data and AI behavior inspectable. Our work spans automated judgment, knowledge graph reasoning, longitudinal interaction and the design choices made by generative systems.

themes.title: Learning and Evaluation in Complex Systems
themes.question: How should relationships, domain knowledge, and interaction shape the way we train and evaluate AI?
themes.description: We build methods and evaluation frameworks for relational and industrial data. Applications in maritime systems, semiconductor manufacturing and recommendation motivate questions about causal structure, robustness and what a useful metric measures.
